rates/axes: A loss curve plots the training loss, L, as training goes on. Its shape says what is wrong.
rates/low: A learning rate too low: the loss falls, but slowly, in an almost straight line.
rates/high: Too high: it drops fast at first, then stalls at a high level, its steps too big to settle into the valley.
rates/huge: Far too high: the loss shoots up, and soon prints nan, not a number.
rates/good: A good rate drops quickly, then keeps creeping lower.
more/noisy: A curve that jumps up and down but still trends lower means each gradient is noisy, usually because the batch is small. A bigger batch smooths it.
more/val: Now add the validation loss. If the training loss keeps falling while validation turns and climbs, the model is overfitting.
more/gap: A small, steady gap between the two is normal. A gap that keeps widening is the warning sign.
more/bottom: The best weights are where validation bottomed out, here at epoch twelve. Keep those, and stop there.
read/list: Often the log is just numbers. Read them as a curve, one point per reading. Here, every hundred steps: two point three oh, two point two eight, two point two six, two point two four.
read/slow: Each reading is about two hundredths lower than the last: the same small drop every time, an almost straight line. The learning rate is too low.
read/plateau: This one falls from two point three oh to one point three eight, then hovers near one point two: a fast drop, then flat at a high level. The rate is too high to settle.
read/explode: This one more than doubles every reading, four point eight eight, eleven point two one, until it prints nan. The rate is far too high.
read/noisy: And this one goes up, down, up, down, but each low is lower than the one before: a noisy curve that still trends down. The batch is too small.
try/p: Try one. Three runs train the same model, differing only in the learning rate. Order them from the lowest rate to the highest.
try/lowest: Run C drops by the same tiny amount each time: the lowest rate.
try/middle: Run A drops fast and keeps going lower: a good rate, in between.
try/highest: Run B blows up to nan: the highest. So C, then A, then B.
